chunks: And it was narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who pays one hundred dirhams in advance for wheat or dates. Then, when the debt becomes due, the seller comes and says, “By Allah, I do not have except half of what is yours; so take from me, if you wish, wheat for half of what is yours and silver coin for the other half.” He said: “There is no harm, if he takes the silver coin from him just as he had given it.”
He said: And I asked him about a man who owes me a basket of unripe dates, and I take from him in its place a basket of fresh dates, while it is less than it. He said: “There is no harm.”

I said: Then a basket of unripe dates is owed to me, and I take in its place a basket of dried dates, while it is more than it. He said: “There is no harm, if it is agreed and known between the two of you.”

He said: And I asked him about a man who has against another one hundred kurrs of dates, and the latter has palm trees. So he comes to him and says, “Give me these palm trees of yours in exchange for what you owe.” Then it was as though he disliked it.

He said: And I asked him about a man who is owed by another loads of fresh dates or dried dates, so he sends dinars to him and says, “Buy with these and take in full for me what is yours.” He said: “There is no harm, if he trusts him.”

key_terms.الدَّيْنُ: the debt or liability that becomes due
key_terms.الْحِنْطَةِ: wheat as the commodity purchased in advance
key_terms.جُلَّةٌ: a basket or measured container of produce
key_terms.يُسْلِمُ: to pay in advance in a salam transaction

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on substituting goods or cash when settling a salam sale or a debt in dates?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings related to salam transactions, repayment in substituted goods, and settlement of debts involving dates and money. It indicates permissibility in certain forms of substitution and repayment when the terms are known and mutually recognized, while showing disapproval toward taking palm trees directly against a date debt.
